text:
nina: Hey all 9 I opened my first PR to add a small cache around model config loads (branch feat/cache/model-config). Two quick newbie questions: do we prefer a single-sentence PR title and a gif/short capture for behavioral changes? Also what's our squash vs preserve-commits norm?

omar: Welcome, nina! :wave: Short answers: keep the PR title concise (ticket + 1 line). GIFs or short recordings are great for UI or observable behavior changes; for backend perf change a short microbenchmark snippet in the body is sufficient.

omar: For commits, iterate with multiple commits while working. Before merge we like a single logical commit on main. You can squash locally or use the repo's squash-on-merge option. If there are valuable intermediate commits (proto work) keep them until the final tidy-up.

nina: Thanks. I ran pre-commit and fixed formatting, but there's still a flaky integration test in CI. How do I signal that on the PR?

omar: Add the label `ci-flake` and paste the failing job URL. If you can reproduce locally, add reproduction steps in the PR body. If you need help, ping #eng-sre or mention me and I'll triage.

review-bot: Tip: include these sections in the PR body: "What/Why", "How to run locally", "Testing done", "Rollback plan".

nina: One more: after the PR merges, will this need a backport to the last stable branch? If so what's the process?

omar: If it's a bugfix for a release branch, add `needs-backport` with the target branch name in the PR description before merging. After merge maintainers will create a backport PR to the target branch. If it's purely perf/internal, usually no backport.

nina: Helpful, thanks! I'll add a short benchmark snippet and the checklist, run pre-commit, and mark ready. Appreciate the quick orientation :pray:
